transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Ethan (CTO - Lodestar), Rina (Head of ML), Carlos (Product), Ava (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for making time, uh quick intro, im maya patel AE for redwood, with liam and sofia from our eng team. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Ethan: good, thanks maya. we wanted to use this to scope a POC for open models for our insights product.
[00:12] Rina: yes, we run financial research summarization, multi-lingual support is needed english spanish french, and some domain fine-tuning might be required.
[00:20] Maya: great, can you walk us through current infra and traffic patterns?
[00:24] Carlos: sure. we have a microservices stack on AWS, requests spike during market open, average payload is short prompts (100-300 tokens) and long prompts for full-article summaries. baseline is about 20 qps average, bursting to 60 qps during peak, so for the POC we'd like to validate ~30-50 qps sustained with <500ms p95 for short prompts.
[00:45] Liam: ok that helps. is data sensitive? e.g., PII or regulated financial data?
[00:49] Rina: yes, client data has account identifiers and some transactional info; we need SOC2, KMS integration, and audit logs. likely VPC peering or private deployment for the pilot.
[01:02] Sofia: quick note on deployment modes - for a POC we can do dedicated hosted instances with VPC peering; Private on-prem is heavier and usually later. V P C sometimes transcribed as VPC in logs but just want to call that out.
[01:16] Ethan: timeline wise, we want results in 4-6 weeks to decide whether to commit to dedicated capacity.
[01:22] Maya: perfect. let's talk success criteria - what are you measuring?
[01:26] Rina: quality is top: for extractive summaries we want ROUGE-L > 0.65 and for classification tasks > 92% accuracy; latency p95 < 500ms for short prompts; cost per 1k requests under our threshold (we'll share target later). Also multilingual parity - we need quality in ES/FR comparable to EN (within ~5% relative).
[01:46] Liam: good. for workload sizing we'll run two benchmark profiles: short prompt (avg 150 tokens) and long summarization (avg 1200 tokens). We'll instrument end-to-end latency including network, so need SRE access.
[01:59] Ava: I can provide a sample data slice and S3 read-only credentials. We'll need instructions for anonymization; we prefer redwood to run against scrubbed logs first.
[02:08] Maya: noted. now model discussion - since you asked for open models, here's a shortlist we typically recommend and why, plus tradeoffs.
[02:16] Liam: list one: Llama-3-chat 13B and 70B variants (instruction tuned) - good balance quality/cost, strong instruction-following, multiling support improving; 70B is obviously higher quality but more expensive and latency higher unless quantized.
[02:33] Liam: list two: Mistral-Mix or Mistral-Chat (high quality for shorter contexts, smaller footprint than 70B, often competitive with larger families on English). limited domain fine-tune availability depends on release.
[02:46] Sofia: list three: Falcon-180B/40B - open family with strong multilingual capabilities, but hardware optimized runtime matters a lot; some kernels are not yet fully optimized which can increase latency.
[02:58] Liam: list four: Mosaic / Redmond community models (e.g., Mixtral) - lightweight and fast, great for cost but may lose domain nuance on financial jargon.
[03:08] Rina: we also use a proprietary in-house classifier for entity redaction. fine-tuning to preserve redaction behavior is important.
[03:14] Maya: tradeoffs - quality vs cost/latency and operations. for POC we usually recommend 2-3 model variants: 1) a high-quality baseline (Llama-3-70B or Falcon-180B quantized), 2) a mid-tier (Llama-3-13B or Mistral-Chat), 3) a fast-low-cost variant (Mixtral/40B) to evaluate fallbacks.
[03:36] Ethan: which models are easiest to run on your dedicated infra?
[03:39] Liam: our runtime supports quantized INT8 and some INT4 paths; we've validated Llama-family and Mistral on our GPU pools. Falcon runs well but depends on kernel selection - we can provision a trial node and run a quick kernel sweep. There's occasional transcription of product names in older notes (e.g., KV cache called K V cache) but we keep track.
[04:02] Carlos: for multilingual we need to measure ES/FR quality; are there off-the-shelf translation mappings or do you recommend training bilingual instruction prompts?
[04:09] Sofia: for many models, prompt engineering and a small in-domain fine-tune (LoRA) on ~5-10k examples closes gaps. We can include that as an optional phase of the POC if you can provide labeled pairs.
[04:21] Rina: data handling constraints - we need audit logs and KMS for keys, plus SSO for the console.
[04:26] Maya: on security: we'll send SOC2 summary, ISO certs, and our KMS integration docs. For onboarding we'll propose VPC peering and ephemeral creds for the bench.
[04:36] Ethan: benchmarks - what metrics will you run?
[04:39] Liam: we plan to measure: p50/p95/p99 latency (split by short/long prompts), throughput (qps), token cost, model quality (ROUGE/EM/accuracy by task), and memory/GPUs required per variant. We'll run synthetic and replay tests with your sample dataset. We'll also capture tail latency to understand cold start effects.
[04:58] Maya: what about KV cache and long-form summarization memory needs?
[05:01] Liam: for long summaries we'll enable prefix caching and chunked pipelines - KV cache sizing depends on sequence length; we'll include memory profiles in the benchmark output. There may be transcription oddities in notes where KV cache is written as K V cache - ignore that.
[05:15] Carlos: timeline again - 6 weeks sounds tight. Can you outline phases?
[05:18] Maya: phase 0: security review and access (week 1); phase 1: baseline benchmarks on three model variants (week 2-3); phase 2: optional LoRA fine-tune and multilingual tests (week 4); phase 3: run production-like replay and finalize report (week 5-6). We can compress to 4 weeks for a lighter scope.
[05:36] Rina: success criteria gating - does the model meet ROUGE/accuracy and hit latency targets; also operational checklist: SSO/KMS/audit logs in place.
[05:45] Liam: we'll provide a metrics dashboard and a CSV export; also include cost projection for 6-week pilot extrapolated to monthly usage.
[05:54] Ava: on networking, VPC peering is our preference; we have strict egress rules, so please share the IP ranges you'll need.
[05:59] Maya: we'll send the peering IP ranges and the onboarding doc.
[06:05] Ethan: about fallback - if quality is lower in ES/FR, can we route those to a larger model only for those requests?
[06:11] Sofia: yes, smart routing is possible - route by language detected, or by confidence threshold; that is one of Redwood's routing features. We'll include an example policy in the bench plan.
[06:22] Carlos: any competitors we've evaluated before? we had a proof-of-concept with Bedrock last year but costs spiked.
[06:28] Maya: noted - we'll include competitor comparison high-level.
[06:31] Liam: regarding hardware, for quantized 70B we typically use A100/NVIDIA H100s with GPU memory optimizations; if we can't get 70B low-latency we fallback to 13B with instruction tuning.
[06:46] Rina: fine-tuning question - do you support LoRA only or full fine-tune?
[06:50] Liam: for POC we recommend LoRA (fast, cheaper) and we can run a controlled full-fine-tune proof if necessary but that costs more and adds time.
[06:59] Carlos: what sample size do you need for fine-tune?
[07:02] Sofia: ~5k to 20k high-quality pairs will show measurable improvements; for classification smaller labeled sets of 1k-2k might suffice.
[07:11] Maya: ok, let's recap next steps.
[07:14] Maya: Maya will send SOC2/ISO summary, pricing options, and peering IP ranges by Friday (2026-03-06).
[07:21] Liam: I'll send the benchmark plan (metrics, harness, model variants to test) and a short sample script for replay tests by 2026-03-08.
[07:28] Ava: I'll share S3 sample data and a sanitized dataset pointer by 2026-03-09.
[07:33] Rina: I'll lock down the success criteria thresholds internally and confirm by 2026-03-06.
[07:38] Ethan: schedule kickoff for week of 2026-03-09, pref mornings PT.
[07:42] Maya: sounds good. any final questions?
[07:45] Carlos: none here. thanks everyone.
[07:47] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with a one-pager and the benchmark plan.
[07:51] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts (model names sometimes truncated, K V cache spaced), speaker labels sometimes generic in our export but cleaned slightly for readability.

End of transcript.
